transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. 

Basically, I'm here because I just keep making these dumb mistakes at work. I supervise a sales team, and lately I'm constantly messing up the sales reports. Like, I'll copy the wrong numbers over from the team dashboard, or I'll completely miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check. And the frustrating thing is, it happens even when I really thought I went over it and checked my work. It's just starting to become a real problem.
Did you have problems with attention or careless mistakes when you were a child?

Yeah, I was actually like this as a kid, too. My mom still talks about it, actually. She remembers getting all these notes from my teachers back in elementary school. They were always saying how I rushed through my assignments and made mistakes, or that I kept losing my homework. And they'd also complain that I talked out of turn a lot, and... well, that I couldn't just stay in my seat without them constantly having to remind me. So, yeah, it's definitely been an issue for a long time.

latest_inference.note: Childhood-onset pattern of careless mistakes, losing homework, talking out of turn, and difficulty staying seated strongly supports ADHD and makes anxiety, depression, stress-related causes, and mild neurocognitive disorder less likely as primary explanations.
